convertibility_reason: Uses external custom signal library ACBC_WS_MFI.mqh with CBC_WS_MFI class - trading logic is encapsulated in an external .mqh file that must be manually interpreted and reimplemented. The standard MQL5 Expert Advisor framework (CExpert, CExpertSignal) is also involved, adding structural complexity.

derived_values.name: CBC_WS_MFI signal composite - weighted MFI vs MA crossover logic

other_exits: Signal-based close when CBC_WS_MFI filter signal crosses Signal_ThresholdClose (10) in opposite direction

custom_logic_notes: The core trading signal logic is entirely encapsulated in the CBC_WS_MFI class from ACBC_WS_MFI.mqh. This class inherits from CExpertSignal and implements LongCondition()/ShortCondition() methods internally. The signal uses MFI(37) with an MA(13) smoothing filter, combined with a weight factor (1.0) and threshold-based open/close decisions. The exact crossover/comparison logic between MFI and its MA, plus any Williams-type bar-by-bar pattern matching (ABC = Awesome Bar Chart pattern), is opaque without reading the .mqh source. CExpert framework handles position checking, validation, and indicator initialization automatically.
python_conversion_notes: The CBC_WS_MFI.mqh file must be located and its LongCondition/ShortCondition logic fully reverse-engineered before Python conversion is possible. The CExpert framework's signal threshold mechanism (0-100 range with open/close thresholds of 10) needs to be replicated. MFI indicator is available in most Python TA libraries (volume-weighted). The MA on MFI is straightforward. Key unknown: whether the 'ABC' component refers to Williams' Awesome Oscillator bar patterns (3-bar momentum sequence) or a custom pattern - must verify in the .mqh. SL/TP of 50 points may need digit-adjustment (multiply by 10 for 5-digit brokers) since the EA uses _Point-based CExpert framework which handles this internally. Expert_EveryTick=false means the EA evaluates on new bar close only, simplifying backtest logic to per-bar evaluation.
